chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who urinates and it hits his thigh and his knee to the extent of a spot of urine, so he prays, then he remembers afterwards that he had not washed it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash it and repeat his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to wash a spot of urine before praying?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for minor impurity (nukta) on the body, establishing that washing the specific contaminated spot and repeating the prayer is sufficient, rather than requiring a full renewal of wudu. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease in purification, distinguishing between impurities on the body versus clothing, and underscores the importance of verifying purity before concluding the prayer.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhmmad, from Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro, from Al Hassan Bin Ziyad who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the man who urinates, so it hits his thigh and his knees, of a measurement of a spot of urine. So he prays Salaat, then he remembers afterwards that he had not washed it. Heasws said: ‘He should wash and he would repeat the Salaat’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr from al-Hassan ibn Ziyad who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about a man whose thigh and knee come in contact with a small drop of urine. He performs Salah (prayer) then remembers that he had not washed it clean? He (the Imam) said, ‘He must perform his Salah (prayer) again.’”
